tytul: Whole sweet cherries in very light syrup (NCHFP)
wstep: This card describes the NCHFP method for canning whole sweet cherries in a very light syrup in a boiling-water bath.

akapity: Choose bright, evenly colored, mature cherries of a quality fit for eating fresh or cooking.
Remove the stems and wash the cherries; removing the pits is optional.
Keep pitted cherries in water with ascorbic acid so they do not darken at the stem end.
If you leave the pits in, prick the skin of each cherry on opposite sides with a clean needle so it does not split.
NCHFP allows water, apple juice, white grape juice or syrup as the liquid; this card uses a very light syrup.
Syrup helps keep the flavor, color and shape of the fruit, but it does not prevent spoilage.
NCHFP uses US measures: a cup holds about 237 ml.

For a very light syrup (about 10% sugar) NCHFP uses 6 1/2 cups of water and 3/4 cup of sugar for a load of 9 pint jars, or 10 1/2 cups of water and 1 1/4 cups of sugar for 7 quart jars; heat the water and sugar together to a boil.
Hot pack: put the drained cherries in a large saucepan, add 1/2 cup of syrup for each quart (about 0.95 l) of fruit and bring to a boil.
Fill the jars with the cherries and cooking liquid, leaving 1/2 inch (about 1.3 cm) of headspace.
Raw pack: pour 1/2 cup of hot syrup into each jar, then fill the jar with drained cherries, shaking it gently as you fill.
Add more hot syrup, leaving 1/2 inch (about 1.3 cm) of headspace.
For both packs, put on the lids and process.
At 0–1000 ft (up to 300 m) process hot-packed pints for 15 minutes and quarts for 20, and raw-packed pints or quarts for 25 minutes.
Above 1000 ft the food may spoil if the time is not increased.
At 1001–3000 ft (above 300 m up to 900 m): hot pack, pints 20 minutes and quarts 25; raw pack, pints or quarts 30 minutes.
At 3001–6000 ft (above 900 m up to 1800 m): hot pack, pints 20 minutes and quarts 30; raw pack, pints or quarts 35 minutes.
Above 6000 ft (above 1800 m): hot pack, pints 25 minutes and quarts 35; raw pack, pints or quarts 40 minutes.
The card converts feet to metres and rounds the limits down, towards the longer time: 1000 ft becomes 300 m, 3000 ft becomes 900 m and 6000 ft becomes 1800 m.
Shortening the time or cooling jars in cold water can also lead to spoilage.
NCHFP times are for US jar sizes: a pint holds about 473 ml and a quart about 946 ml.
JarAtlas rule (NCHFP does not test metric jars): for a jar of up to 473 ml use the pint time, and for a larger jar of up to 946 ml, for example 0.5 l or 0.9 l, use the quart time.
This NCHFP recipe gives no time for jars larger than a quart, such as 1 l, so JarAtlas recommends smaller jars.
